🌐 Web query:

`Does navigator.clipboard become undefined (not a rejected promise) in an insecure context in current Chrome and Firefox?`

💡 Result:

Yes, in both current Chrome and Firefox, the navigator.clipboard property is undefined when the page is served in an insecure context (such as HTTP) [1][2][3]. The Clipboard API is restricted to secure contexts (HTTPS) as a security measure to protect user data [4][5][6]. Because it is not available, the browser does not provide a rejected promise; instead, the navigator.clipboard property itself is absent from the navigator object, which often results in a TypeError (e.g., "Cannot read properties of undefined") if code attempts to access it without checking for its existence first [2][7][3]. To safely implement clipboard functionality, it is standard practice to check for the property's existence and the security status of the context before usage [1][2][5]: if (navigator.clipboard && window.isSecureContext) { // Safe to use navigator.clipboard await navigator.clipboard.writeText('...'); } else { // Fallback to insecure methods or inform the user }

Citations:

- 1: https://stackoverflow.com/questions/51805395/navigator-clipboard-is-undefined
- 2: https://stackoverflow.com/questions/71873824/copy-text-to-clipboard-cannot-read-properties-of-undefined-reading-writetext
- 3: https://bobbyhadz.com/blog/navigator-clipboard-is-undefined-in-javascript
- 4: https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Navigator/clipboard
- 5: https://web.dev/articles/async-clipboard
- 6: https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Clipboard_API
- 7: https://stackoverflow.com/questions/55654479/clipboard-api-read-write-paste-on-a-non-ssl-site

**Guard against an unavailable `navigator.clipboard`.**

In an insecure context, `navigator.clipboard` is undefined. Accessing `.writeText` throws before `.catch()` is created, so the button remains in its idle state. Set `"failed"` and return before calling `writeText`.
